data.reason: Review returns the ticket. Two findings at high severity are changes to the tree a session must make before merge: F1, adding the hook copies to generated_paths() also drops .claude/settings.json out of the code fingerprint the review gate compares, so the permission allowlist and defaultMode can move between triage and advance with nothing refusing it, which re-opens for the one file holding a security control the hole SEEN-107 closed for every other; and F2, PreCompact and SubagentStop are withheld from Codex on a reason record 20 proved false from the codex-cli schemas, with a passing test now holding the false reason in place. Criterion 5 is unmet and only a live Codex session settles it, which on its own would hold the ticket at review rather than return it; the return is for F1 and F2, and hooks.json should be decided before that session runs so the one observation covers the events as corrected rather than as shipped.

findings.claim: Adding the two hook copies to generated_paths() also removes .claude/settings.json from the code fingerprint the review gate compares, so the permission allowlist and defaultMode can change between the triage and the review advance with nothing refusing it and no focus set naming it.
findings.failure_scenario: generated_paths() feeds procedure_paths(), which gates._require_the_diff_has_not_moved passes to repository.fingerprint(excluding=...). A session runs the triage, then before harness advance adds a Bash(curl:*) entry to permissions.allow or sets defaultMode to bypassPermissions in .claude/settings.json. The file was unchanged at triage time so it is in no focus set; the code fingerprint now excludes it so the diff-has-not-moved check reads unmoved; doctor cannot see it because hooks.drift compares only the entries whose command begins with the harness invocation and the permissions block is generated by nothing; and the review advance then attests a tree carrying a widened permission surface that no reviewer read. This is the hole F4 of SEEN-107's review closed for every other file, re-opened for the one file that holds a security control. The wholly generated skill and agent copies do not have this property, because agents.drift and skills.drift compare their full text.

findings.claim: PreCompact and SubagentStop are withheld from Codex on a stated reason this ticket's own record 20 records as disproved from the codex-cli schemas, and harness/tests/test_hooks.py:164 asserts the withholding with that false reason as its rationale, so the correction now has to argue with a passing test.
findings.failure_scenario: The source says Codex documents no compaction hook (line 46) and Codex has no subagent-stop event (line 59). Record 20 reports both events present in the per-event JSON Schemas inside the codex-cli 0.156.1 binary. A Codex session that compacts writes no handoff pack, which is the loss PreCompact exists to prevent, and a Codex reviewer's findings are never held to the review gate's rule before advance. A later session that corrects clients to include codex sees test_the_codex_copy_takes_no_event_codex_does_not_document fail and reads a correct change as a regression. One of the two must happen before merge: a generated source whose recorded reason is known false is worse than either behaviour, and a test is now holding the false one in place.

findings.claim: PreCompact writes a handoff record that kpi.slice_windows reads as a slice boundary keyed by slice.done, so an automatic pack silently overwrites an earlier slice's recorded token cost with a fragment of the current slice's spending.
findings.failure_scenario: kpi._closes (harness/kpi.py:186) returns data['slice']['done'] for every handoff record and reads nothing of the new data['auto'] flag. A session declares its boundary after slice 1 (done=1, figures A), so windows[1] holds A. It works on into slice 2 and a compaction fires: current_slice infers done=1 again, so the auto record carries done=1 and windows[1] is rewritten as the tokens spent between the boundary and the compaction, while slice 2's own window later opens at the compaction and is short by the same amount. A compaction during slice 1 instead has done=0, which keys no window but moves the open cursor, so slice 1's cost is understated. Those figures are what SEEN-109's calibration window decides the routes on. Record 20 discloses the understatement and not the overwrite.

findings.claim: _subagent_stop fails closed on a payload field the module admits is unverified, while every other handler in the module fails open, so a missing or renamed last_assistant_message blocks the reviewer on every review instead of letting it through.
findings.failure_scenario: review_in(payload.get('last_assistant_message') or '') returns None for an absent field exactly as it does for an answer with no JSON, and the next line blocks with 'This review carries no JSON review record'. If Claude Code does not send that key under that name, every seen-reviewer subagent is told its correct answer carried no record and has to answer again, which costs one whole extra review answer per review and is the cost this hook was written to save. paths_in, _agent_that_stopped and _pre_compact all allow on an absence; this one refuses on the same class of absence. The fixtures cannot tell, because subagent_stop_payload supplies the field it is testing for.

findings.claim: Two files were changed outside the file list of the slice that changed them, and a journal note was used where the solution record itself named a return to solution as the remedy.
findings.failure_scenario: harness/tests/helpers.py is named by no slice and by no changes entry, which is the triage's slice_files failure, and harness/guard.py was changed in slice 3 whose list does not name it. Both changes are correct and necessary, but the remedy the solution record named for this case, an amendment through a return to solution, was not used either time. slice_files fails, which forces this review to full depth, and a precedent that a note substitutes for an amendment makes the check fail on every harness ticket, so the calibration window records the narrowing as never able to save anything.

findings.claim: No handoff boundary was recorded between slices 2 and 3, so this ticket's own slice windows charge both to slice 2 and slice 3 reads as having cost nothing.
findings.failure_scenario: The journal holds one handoff, record 14 after slice 1, and one session id across all 23 records at 129,413 output tokens against the 60,000 output_token_budget. kpi.slice_windows keys windows[1] from record 14 and then windows[2] from the tdd advance at record 22 with last+1, so the window from record 14 to record 22 carries slices 2 and 3 together and windows[3] is never keyed. The sprint report will show slice 3, the two-point slice, at no cost.

findings.claim: Criterion 2 asks for the refusals proven with hook-input fixtures for both assistants, and only the outside-slice rule is reached through a payload; the stage rule, the branch rule and the two allowances are proven through the command alone.
findings.failure_scenario: PreToolUseTest exercises the slice-files refusal with a Claude Edit payload and with both Codex apply_patch shapes, and nothing exercises a clarify or solution refusal, a non-ticket-branch refusal, or the ticket-file and drafts allowance through either payload. The composition is sound today because _pre_tool_use and guard_command resolve the branch and the journal the same way, so the gap is not a wrong result now. It becomes one the moment a payload shape carries something the guard should read beyond the path, for instance a rename where only the destination is checked: a Move to: header is read by _patched but nothing asserts which side of a rename is judged.

findings.claim: Two documentation facts do not match the evidence this ticket gathered: the hooks row says Codex has the same thirteen events, and CLAUDE.md's harness command list still omits guard and hook.
findings.failure_scenario: Record 20 and the hooks.py docstring both say twenty-three schemas, and the events they name come to twelve, so thirteen is a figure the journal's own evidence does not support and a later session looking for the thirteenth finds nothing. Separately, CLAUDE.md enumerates every harness command and now names neither of the two this ticket added, so a session that reads the rules rather than the skill does not know it can ask whether an edit is allowed before making it.
